text:
maria: Customer reported intermittent failures when using the TS SDK in JSON streaming mode. Error is 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token' on the client when trying to parse stream frames. Happening more under load. cc @dan :eyes:

support-bot: Ticket CS-4621 created for this report (priority: P2).

dan: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro + raw chunk/log where parsing fails? Is the customer using a custom delimiter or the SDK default?

maria: They're using a double-newline delimiter ("\n\n") because payloads can be multi-line. Repro (simplified):

```ts
const stream = client.responses.stream({
  model: 'redwood/fast-13b',
  mode: 'json',
  delimiter: '\n\n'
});
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  // naive approach the customer used
  const frame = chunk.toString();
  JSON.parse(frame); // throws sometimes
}
```

Raw capture from their tcp sniff (split across frames):
```
frame #42: '{"msg":"ok","id":42}\n\n{"msg":"up',
frame #43: 'date","id":43}\n\n'
```
When frame #42 arrives and they call JSON.parse on it immediately, it's fine. But sometimes the TCP boundary splits inside a JSON object:
```
frame #51: '{"msg":"partial","id":51\n',
frame #52: '}'
```
They attempt to parse frame #51 alone and get: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` or occasionally `Unexpected token }` depending on how the client concatenates frames.

ingrid: Sounds like the framing/delimiter handling in the TS SDK is trying to drain on separators but doesn't guarantee that a complete JSON object is assembled before parse. If a delimiter appears at the start of the next frame (e.g., an empty frame) the naive parser might attempt to parse an empty string -> `Unexpected token` errors.

ryan-q: Agreed. Also edge cases with CRLF vs LF can cause an extra empty-frame. Customer uses a mix of Windows/macos producers so we should normalize.

maria: Customer logs show a stacktrace: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 0 at JSON.parse (<anonymous>) at handleChunk (app.js:123:15)` — they point at our SDK user callback but the root cause looks like framing.

dan: Can you ask the customer to try two quick workarounds and report back?
1) Switch to text mode and parse with an incremental/ndjson parser in userland.
2) As a quick SDK workaround, buffer chunks until `try { JSON.parse(buffered) } catch(e) { /* wait for more */ }` rather than parsing per chunk.

maria: Sent the workarounds. They replied that buffering fixed it for short-term. They also ran a simple fuzz that reproduces the bug reliably: split objects at random byte offsets and feed to the SDK stream consumer — parsing fails ~22% of runs.

ingrid: I'll add a unit test in the TS SDK that simulates split-frame delivery and ensure the internal framing logic never attempts to parse an empty or partial frame. Probable fix: make the delimiter scanner accumulate until a non-empty token separated by delimiter is present and trim leading/trailing empty tokens. Also handle CRLF normalization before splitting.

dan: Good plan. Create an internal issue and link CS-4621. Also we should backport a patch to the last two releases since customers might be on older SDKs.

maria: Created internal bug: ENG-SDK-1259. Added repro harness and the customer's sample pcap. Noted workaround in ticket.

ryan-q: One more thought: streaming JSON mode should expose a helper that returns complete parsed frames as objects (like an async generator of objects) so users don't need to implement buffering incorrectly. Let's track that as an enhancement.

maria: Customer will try the patched build we attach to the ticket tomorrow. I'll follow up once they confirm. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Updated CS-4621: status -> awaiting-customer.

dan: Thanks team. Assigning ENG-SDK-1259 to @ingrid for fix + tests.

ingrid: Taking it. I'll push a branch with tests today and ping for a review when ready.

maria: Closing loop: they were able to run our branch and the parsing errors disappeared during their 2h load test. Marking CS-4621 as 'resolved (patch)'.

ryan-q: Nice! We'll RFC the helper API later.

maria: Filing postmortem checklist item: add e2e streaming split-frame tests to CI to prevent regressions.
